The harbor log for the autumn

  • Harbor
  • Moorings
  • Tides
  • Council

The harbor office keeps a log of every boat that passes the north light, and the log for the autumn shows more traffic than any season before it.

Most of the new traffic is small boats that fish the outer banks in the morning and come back before the afternoon wind rises over the quay.

The office asks the crews to call in when they pass the light, so the watch can count them, and most of them do so without being asked twice.

On the busiest days the watch counted more than forty boats before noon, and the moorings on the inner quay were full well before dusk fell.

The council has asked the office whether the quay needs more moorings, and the office has answered that it needs a second watch before it does.

A second watch would let the office keep the light open later in the evening, when the crews that fish the far banks come back to the harbor.

The council will decide in the spring, after the office has counted the boats for another season and written its report on the winter tides.

Until then the office keeps its hours, and asks the crews to plan their return so that they pass the light before the watch goes off duty.
